title: SSO attribute precedence causing unexpected deny/fallthrough and missing audit annotations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer reported two related failures after SSO group sync: 1) engineers were denied access to routes they should have via a nested group; 2) several admin elevation events that should have been logged with the reason field are missing audit annotations (reason=null). Both surfaced after RBAC v2 migration and appear tied to attribute precedence and fallback behavior in our SAML attribute processor. This ticket captures triage, proposed fix, and rollout plan.
reproduction_steps: 1) Configure IdP to send nestedGroup and primaryGroup claims in SAML assertion (primaryGroup absent for some sessions).
2) Onboard test user U with primaryGroup omitted but nestedGroup present (mapped to a role with route permission allow).
3) Trigger login; observe RBAC evaluation path: fallback to default precedence, then deny returned instead of allow.
4) Separately, simulate service account token exchange flow that triggers admin elevation; check /audit/events for new entries and note reason field is empty for >10% of events.
impact_summary: High — multiple enterprise customers escalated for permission denied in production during normal SSO flows; missing audit reason breaks compliance reporting for 3 customers (SOC2/Audit). Affects hosted and Dedicated customers using SAML group sync and role mapping rules. Potential to cause user productivity loss and audit failure for regulated customers.
root_cause: RBAC v2 attribute resolution merges SAML attributes in the following order: explicit role bindings -> idp_groups -> cached_group_membership. When primary assertions are missing, fallback logic incorrectly treats absent primaryGroup as higher-precedence 'empty' value, masking nestedGroup-derived bindings. Additionally, during a code-path where we synthesize an 'admin' escalation for service tokens we neglected to populate the audit 'reason' annotation when the elevation came via the fallback branch. Race between group-sync cache updates and assertion processing can surface both issues.
mitigation: Temporary emergency mitigation deployed: revert fallback precedence to previous stable ordering for assertion parsing (hotfix v0.0.7) and enable verbose audit write for all admin-elevation events. Communicated to affected customers with rollout of hotfix and requested SSO session re-login. Note: hotfix increases attribute resolution latency slightly; monitoring dashboards updated.
proposed_fix: 1) Fix attribute precedence algorithm: treat absent attributes as 'missing' and continue evaluating lower-precedence attributes instead of assigning an empty value; add unit tests covering nestedGroup/primaryGroup permutations. 2) Ensure audit logging writes 'reason' field on all admin elevation code paths; add end-to-end test that inflates audit events and asserts payload schema. 3) Add canary and rollout with traffic-splitting (5% -> 25% -> 100%) and hooks to automatically rollback on elevated audit error rates or auth failure spikes.
acceptance_criteria: All unit and integration tests for attribute precedence pass (primaryGroup present/absent/nested combos).
Reproduced customer repro no longer fails in staging and smoke tests show allow behavior restored.
Audit events for admin elevation contain non-empty 'reason' and match schema in >99.95% of sampled events during 24h canary.
No regression in SSO latencies beyond accepted threshold (p95 increase <= 25ms).
Runbook updated with steps for emergency rollback and customer-facing communication template.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy to staging and run synthetic logins for 6 hours; validate acceptance criteria.
Stage 2: Canary deploy to 5% of production login traffic (select non-critical customer cohort) for 12 hours; monitor auth failures, audit schema errors, latency.
Stage 3: Expand to 25% for 24 hours if metrics stable; collect customer feedback from those cohorts.
Stage 4: Full rollout to 100% with increased monitoring retention for 72 hours; prepare rollback tag and automation.
Rollback: revert to v0.0.7-hotfix ordering if auth failure or missing audit reasons exceed thresholds.
